merger_name: Jellinbah Group - Further interest in Lake Vermont JV
merger_description:
Jellinbah Group, through a wholly-owned subsidiary QCMM (Lake Vermont Holdings) Pty Ltd, is proposing to acquire an additional 10% interest in the unincorporated joint venture that owns and operates the Lake Vermont coal mine in Queensland’s Bowen Basin (**Lake Vermont JV**) from a subsidiary of Sojitz Corporation (**Sojitz**) (the **Acquisition**). As part of the Acquisition, Jellinbah Group will also acquire an additional 10% of the shares in Bowen Basin Coal Pty Ltd, an entity that holds the Lake Vermont JV’s mining tenements.

The Lake Vermont JV primarily produces metallurgical coal, as well as small volumes of thermal coal, most of which it exports to customers overseas.

In addition to its existing 70% interest in the Lake Vermont JV, Jellinbah Group holds a 70% interest in the joint venture that owns and operates the Jellinbah coal mine in Queensland’s Bowen Basin. Jellinbah Group is controlled by Zashvin Pty Ltd, a private investment company.

Sojitz is a multinational general trading company incorporated in Japan. In Australia, Sojitz holds interests in several mining projects (including coal projects), as well investments in the renewable energy, infrastructure and transport sectors. Sojitz is divesting its full interest in the Lake Vermont JV.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided by the applicant, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. Jellinbah Group is already a majority interest holder in the
Lake Vermont JV, and the Acquisition would increase
Jellinbah Group’s existing majority interest holding
b. the Acquisition is expected to have limited impact on
domestic sales of coal in Australia
c. there are alternative suppliers of both metallurgical and
thermal coal in Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
